title: Exchanging a Leopard Cat for a Prince

series.title: Exchanging a Leopard Cat for a Prince

fullText.simplified:
第四十一章、世间大义

    真相已经大白，包拯说，八王爷和太后犯的都是死罪。皇帝听了，让所有人都退下，只留了包拯一个人。
    皇帝走下龙椅，来到包拯面前，和他面对面站着。
    “包拯，我想八王爷和太后都活着。”
    “皇上，您说过，您会公正处理。”包拯直视着皇帝的眼睛。
    “是的，我说过，但是刀没有落到自己身上的时候，永远不知道那会有多疼。”
    “您感觉到疼了，那楚珠、马超、蓝香，还有高小山，他们就不知道疼吗？勇气是什么？是虽然知道会疼，但还是去做！在有些人眼里，他们也许只是不重要的小人物，但他们知道正义比个人生死更重要，他们比很多人都高大！他们做的事情是世间大义！”包拯一字一句问道：“如果现在他们站在这儿，皇上——嘴里说着要公正处理的皇上，您要怎么面对他们呢？”
    “包拯，你好大的胆子……”皇帝盯着包拯，握紧了手心。
    包拯迎着皇帝有些生气的目光，用更大的声音再一字一句地问道：“如果！李妃娘娘站在这儿！您要怎么面对她呢？”
    怒气消退，悲伤重回脸上，皇帝的肩松下去。他转过身去，背向包拯，深深地沉默了。
    不知过了多久，门外远远传来一声钟响，天亮了。
    皇帝终于转过身来。包拯还是直直地站着，脸上是不低头、不退让的表情。
    “好了，包拯，你别这个样子了，我知道了，你骂得对。”皇帝说。
    包拯不说话，表情也没有变化，他在坚定地等一个答案。
    皇帝沉重说道：“张怀死罪。太后从今天起入冷宫，余生都在冷宫中度过。八王爷不再是王爷，他将搬出王府，做个普通人。”他拍了拍包拯的肩：“我知道你还有话说，但都不要说了，这是我的决定。”
    包拯没有说话，他跪下去，从衣服里拿出皇帝的令牌，双手举到皇帝面前：“皇上，这个令牌还给您，我要回家了。”
    皇帝看着包拯低下去的头，表情有些复杂。他没有接，也没有说话，大殿里安静极了。包拯等了很久，才听到皇帝的声音：“包拯，这个令牌，只要我没有要你还，你就要永远拿着。这个案子虽然破了，但还有很多案子等着你。没有我的命令，你哪儿都不能去，知道了吗？”
    包拯沉默了一会儿，回答道：“我知道了。”
    “那你起来吧。”皇帝说。
    包拯站起身，低头问：“现在我可以回家了吗？”
    “不可以，你还要带我去个地方。”
    包拯抬头，看着脸上再次露出悲伤的皇帝，心中马上明白了。
    “好的，皇上。”他弯腰道。
fullText.traditional:
第四十一章、世間大義

    真相已經大白，包拯說，八王爺和太后犯的都是死罪。皇帝聽了，讓所有人都退下，只留了包拯一個人。
    皇帝走下龍椅，來到包拯面前，和他面對面站著。
    “包拯，我想八王爺和太后都活著。”
    “皇上，您說過，您會公正處理。”包拯直視著皇帝的眼睛。
    “是的，我說過，但是刀沒有落到自己身上的時候，永遠不知道那會有多疼。”
    “您感覺到疼了，那楚珠、馬超、藍香，還有高小山，他們就不知道疼嗎？勇氣是什麼？是雖然知道會疼，但還是去做！在有些人眼裡，他們也許只是不重要的小人物，但他們知道正義比個人生死更重要，他們比很多人都高大！他們做的事情是世間大義！”包拯一字一句問道：“如果現在他們站在這兒，皇上——嘴裡說著要公正處理的皇上，您要怎麼面對他們呢？”
    “包拯，你好大的膽子……”皇帝盯著包拯，握緊了手心。
    包拯迎著皇帝有些生氣的目光，用更大的聲音再一字一句地問道：“如果！李妃娘娘站在這兒！您要怎麼面對她呢？”
    怒氣消退，悲傷重回臉上，皇帝的肩鬆下去。他轉過身去，背向包拯，深深地沉默了。
    不知過了多久，門外遠遠傳來一聲鐘響，天亮了。
    皇帝終於轉過身來。包拯還是直直地站著，臉上是不低頭、不退讓的表情。
    “好了，包拯，你別這個樣子了，我知道了，你罵得對。”皇帝說。
    包拯不說話，表情也沒有變化，他在堅定地等一個答案。
    皇帝沉重說道：“張懷死罪。太后從今天起入冷宮，餘生都在冷宮中度過。八王爺不再是王爺，他將搬出王府，做個普通人。”他拍了拍包拯的肩：“我知道你還有話說，但都不要說了，這是我的決定。”
    包拯沒有說話，他跪下去，從衣服裡拿出皇帝的令牌，雙手舉到皇帝面前：“皇上，這個令牌還給您，我要回家了。”
    皇帝看著包拯低下去的頭，表情有些複雜。他沒有接，也沒有說話，大殿裡安靜極了。包拯等了很久，才聽到皇帝的聲音：“包拯，這個令牌，只要我沒有要你還，你就要永遠拿著。這個案子雖然破了，但還有很多案子等著你。沒有我的命令，你哪兒都不能去，知道了嗎？”
    包拯沉默了一會兒，回答道：“我知道了。”
    “那你起來吧。”皇帝說。
    包拯站起身，低頭問：“現在我可以回家了嗎？”
    “不可以，你還要帶我去個地方。”
    包拯抬頭，看著臉上再次露出悲傷的皇帝，心中馬上明白了。
    “好的，皇上。”他彎腰道。

sentences.simplified: “包拯，这个令牌，只要我没有要你还，你就要永远拿着。
sentences.traditional: “包拯，這個令牌，只要我沒有要你還，你就要永遠拿著。
sentences.pinyin: bāo zhěng zhè ge lìng pái zhǐ yào wǒ méi yǒu yào nǐ huán nǐ jiù yào yǒng yuǎn ná zhe
sentences.english: “Bao Zheng, as long as I don’t ask for it back, you must keep this token forever.

sentences.simplified: 这个案子虽然破了，但还有很多案子等着你。
sentences.traditional: 這個案子雖然破了，但還有很多案子等著你。
sentences.pinyin: zhè ge àn zi suī rán pò le dàn hái yǒu hěn duō àn zi děng zhe nǐ
sentences.english: Although this case is solved, there are still many other cases waiting for you.

sentences.simplified: 没有我的命令，你哪儿都不能去，知道了吗？”
sentences.traditional: 沒有我的命令，你哪兒都不能去，知道了嗎？”
sentences.pinyin: méi yǒu wǒ de mìng lìng nǐ nǎ'r dōu bù néng qù zhī dào le ma
sentences.english: Without my command, you’re not going anywhere. Do you understand?”

sentences.simplified: 包拯沉默了一会儿，回答道：“我知道了。”
sentences.traditional: 包拯沉默了一會兒，回答道：“我知道了。”
sentences.pinyin: bāo zhěng chén mò le yí huì'r huí dá dào wǒ zhī dào le
sentences.english: Bao Zheng was silent for a moment before he replied, “I understand.”

sentences.simplified: “那你起来吧。”皇帝说。
sentences.traditional: “那你起來吧。”皇帝說。
sentences.pinyin: nà nǐ qǐ lái ba huáng dì shuō
sentences.english: “Then you can get up,” the emperor said.

sentences.simplified: 包拯站起身，低头问：“现在我可以回家了吗？”
sentences.traditional: 包拯站起身，低頭問：“現在我可以回家了嗎？”
sentences.pinyin: bāo zhěng zhàn qǐ shēn dī tóu wèn xiàn zài wǒ kě yǐ huí jiā le ma
sentences.english: Bao Zheng stood up, bowed his head, and asked, “Can I go home now?”

sentences.simplified: “不可以，你还要带我去个地方。”
sentences.traditional: “不可以，你還要帶我去個地方。”
sentences.pinyin: bù kě yǐ nǐ hái yào dài wǒ qù ge dì fang
sentences.english: “No, you still have to take me somewhere.”

sentences.simplified: 包拯抬头，看着脸上再次露出悲伤的皇帝，心中马上明白了。
sentences.traditional: 包拯抬頭，看著臉上再次露出悲傷的皇帝，心中馬上明白了。
sentences.pinyin: bāo zhěng tái tóu kàn zhe liǎn shang zài cì lòu chū bēi shāng de huáng dì xīn zhōng mǎ shàng míng bai le
sentences.english: Bao Zheng looked up, and seeing the emperor’s face fill with sorrow once again, he immediately understood.

sentences.simplified: “好的，皇上。”他弯腰道。
sentences.traditional: “好的，皇上。”他彎腰道。
sentences.pinyin: hǎo de huáng shang tā wān yāo dào
sentences.english: “Very well, Your Majesty,” he said, bowing.

sentence_translations: Chapter 41: Great Justice to This World
The truth had been revealed. Bao Zheng said that both the Eighth Prince and the empress dowager had committed capital offenses.
After hearing this, the emperor ordered everyone to withdraw, leaving only Bao Zheng behind.
The emperor stepped down from the imperial throne. He came to Bao Zheng and stood face-to-face with him.
“Bao Zheng, I want the Eighth Prince and the empress dowager to live.”
“Your Majesty, you said before that you would handle this impartially,” Bao Zheng stared straight into the emperor’s eyes.
“Yes, I did say that, but you never know how painful it is until the blade falls on yourself.”
“You feel the pain, but do you think Chu Zhu, Ma Chao, Lan Xiang, and Gao Xiaoshan don’t know what pain is?
What is courage? It’s doing something despite knowing that it will be painful!
In the eyes of some, they may just be unimportant little people.
But, they know that justice is more important than their own life or death.
They are more noble than many people! What they did was a great justice to this world!”
Bao Zheng asked word by word, ..
.. “If they were standing here now, Your Majesty—the emperor who claims to handle matters impartially, how would you face them?”
“Bao Zheng, you have quite the nerve …” the emperor stared at Bao Zheng, clenching his fist.
Bao Zheng met the emperor’s somewhat angry gaze, and asked again, word by word, in a louder voice, ..
.. “What if! Consort Li was standing here! How would you face her?”
The anger subsided, and sadness returned to his face. The emperor’s shoulders relaxed.
He turned around, his back facing Bao Zheng. He fell into a deep silence.
After some time, a bell rang in the distance outside the door. Dawn had arrived.
The emperor finally turned around.
Bao Zheng still stood tall, and his face had an expression of neither bowing down nor backing down.
“Alright, Bao Zheng, stop acting like this. I understand now. You are right to scold me,” the emperor said.
Bao Zheng did not speak, and his facial expression did not change either. He was steadfastly waiting for an answer.
The emperor said gravely, “Zhang Huai is guilty of a capital offense.
The empress dowager will enter the Cold Palace starting today and will spend the rest of her life there.
The Eighth Prince will no longer be a prince. He will move out of the prince’s mansion and become an ordinary person.
He patted Bao Zheng on the shoulder: “I know you have more to say, but don’t say it. This is my decision.”
Bao Zheng did not say anything.
He knelt down, took out the emperor’s token from his clothes, and held it in front of the emperor with both hands.
“Your Majesty, I am returning this token to you. I am going home.”
The emperor looked at Bao Zheng’s bowed head. His expression was quite complex.
He didn’t accept the token, nor did he say anything. The audience hall was extremely quiet.
Bao Zheng waited for a long time before he finally heard the emperor’s voice.
“Bao Zheng, as long as I don’t ask for it back, you must keep this token forever.
Although this case is solved, there are still many other cases waiting for you.
Without my command, you’re not going anywhere. Do you understand?”
Bao Zheng was silent for a moment before he replied, “I understand.”
“Then you can get up,” the emperor said.
Bao Zheng stood up, bowed his head, and asked, “Can I go home now?”
“No, you still have to take me somewhere.”
Bao Zheng looked up, and seeing the emperor’s face fill with sorrow once again, he immediately understood.
“Very well, Your Majesty,” he said, bowing.
